findings.summary: Spec §1.1 (corpus must reach the role prompt through the positional argument) is not wired on any production path. buildGenerateRoleArgv has zero callers outside test/generate.test.ts, and GenerateDeps.spawnRole takes a structured corpus object with no production implementation anywhere in src/ (no default agent-run dispatch analogous to spawnAgentRunWorker at src/tick-run.ts:774-798). Nothing in the engine ever turns a corpus into argv, so the invariant the package exists to establish is unenforced dead code.

Gate D1 is unmet and has no power over real behaviour. Neither D1 case uses a fake agent-run recording argv, and neither starts from a production entry: the first calls the pure helper buildGenerateRoleArgv directly, and the second captures the corpus handed to a mocked spawnRole and then calls serializeCorpusToPositional itself inside the test, so it passes even if the engine never places corpus text in a positional argument.

Mutation M1 was not applied as specified ("remove the corpus from the positional args"); it was applied to serializeCorpusToPositional, a helper unreachable from production. The reported 2-assertion kill therefore attests only to the test asserting on its own helper's output, not to protection of the §1.1 invariant, and the dev-note nonetheless records D1 as satisfied "from the production entry".

The D3 role/route assertion is tautological: it compares DEFAULT_GENERATE_CONFIG against the same literals hardcoded in src/generate.ts:39-44, with no evidence the values were read from agent-runtime's profiles/routes.yaml and profiles/roles/ as spec §2.1 demands ("do not guess from this document").
An anchor-check failure is silently recorded as verificationRate 0 in the report head, making a crashed check indistinguishable from a genuine 0% verification rate in the exported report.

deriveDocKind classifies every role other than the exact string "dr-synthesizer" as "argument", so a renamed or mistyped synthesizer role silently downgrades a report to an argument instead of failing loudly.

The dev-note header records input_commit df0e4596837a5c81d696f55a4f41f4b60be515c5, which does not match the dispatch's target base ee4a1e39ad0d1f2480d0555496e3b88f923022ba named as the prerequisite in spec line 5; the evidence lineage is inconsistent with the reviewed one.
